email.title: Email
email.subtitle: The SMTP server Sprint Boot sends invitations, password resets and notifications through.
email.sslHint: Turn on for port 465. On other ports the connection upgrades to TLS when the server offers it.
email.passwordKept: Saved. Leave blank to keep it.
email.testHint: Uses the saved settings, so save your changes first.

tokens.title: API & MCP tokens
tokens.apiHint: Let scripts and integrations call the REST API as you.
tokens.mcpHint: Let AI assistants work in Sprint Boot as you, through MCP tools.
tokens.createdHint: This is the only time the token is shown. Store it somewhere safe.
tokens.revokeBody: Anything using this token stops working right away.

clientHint.codex: Run both lines in a terminal, then open a new one so Codex sees {{variable}}. On macOS or Linux, use export {{variable}}=... in your shell profile instead of setx.
clientHint.copilot: Save as .vscode/mcp.json in your project, or add it to your user mcp.json, then start the server from the MCP view in VS Code.
clientHint.config: For Cursor (~/.cursor/mcp.json) and other clients that read an mcpServers file.

mcp.createdConnect: Add the server to your client with one of these. They already hold the new token.
mcp.title: MCP Documentation
mcp.intro: The Model Context Protocol lets AI assistants use tools. With an MCP token, an assistant can read and update your work in Sprint Boot, with exactly the permissions you have.
mcp.connectHint: Create an MCP token, then add this server to your client and replace YOUR_MCP_TOKEN.
mcp.toolsHint: Read tools work with every MCP token. Write tools need a token that is not read only.

tools.list_spaces: Lists the spaces you can see, with their keys.
tools.search_tickets: Finds tickets by text, optionally within one space.
tools.get_ticket: Reads one ticket with its description, comments and subtasks.
tools.list_transitions: Lists the statuses a ticket can move to now.
tools.create_ticket: Creates a ticket in a space.
tools.update_ticket: Changes the title or description of a ticket.
tools.transition_ticket: Moves a ticket to another status, following its workflow.
tools.add_comment: Adds a comment to a ticket.

mcp.securityBody: A token acts as you, so workflow rules and space permissions still apply. Keep tokens out of shared files, give each client its own, and revoke one as soon as it is no longer needed.

globalTemplates.deleteUsed_other: {{count}} space templates reuse it and will be deleted too. Tickets already created from them keep their description.

assistant.title: Assistant
assistant.empty: Ask about your tickets: find them, summarize them, explain what they mean. Changes only happen after you confirm them.
assistant.emptyTicket: Ask about this ticket. The assistant reads it, with its comments, before it answers.
assistant.question: Ask the assistant
assistant.refused: The model declined to answer this.
assistant.cutOff: The answer was cut off at the length limit.
assistant.deleteBody: The conversation is removed for good. Changes it made to tickets stay.
assistant.unavailable: The assistant is switched off. An administrator can turn it on under Administration → AI assistant.
assistant.connectionLost: The connection to the server dropped while the assistant was answering. What it saved is shown; ask again to continue.

assistantAdmin.title: AI assistant
assistantAdmin.subtitle: Let people chat with an AI model about their tickets. The assistant uses the default connection.
assistantAdmin.enabledHint: Everyone signed in can use it. It sees and changes only what each person may, and changes need their confirmation.
assistantAdmin.noConnection: Add a connection, or the assistant stays unavailable.
assistantAdmin.name: Name
assistantAdmin.baseUrlHint: The address of the chat completions API: https://api.openai.com/v1, http://localhost:11434/v1 for Ollama, https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, …

assistantAdmin.modelsLoaded_one: {{count}} model loaded. Pick one from the Model field.
assistantAdmin.modelsLoaded_other: {{count}} models loaded. Pick one from the Model field.
assistantAdmin.noModels: The provider returned no models. Type the model name.
assistantAdmin.deleteBody: If it is the default, another connection becomes the default.
assistantAdmin.privacy: Questions, and the tickets the assistant reads to answer them, are sent to the provider of the default connection.
assistantAdmin.maxRequestKbHint: For gateways that reject large requests (HTTP 413), such as chatgpt2api behind nginx: long conversations then leave out their older messages to fit. Leave empty for OpenAI, Anthropic and most servers.
assistantAdmin.maxOutputTokensHint: The longest answer the model may write in one turn, in tokens. Empty uses the default: 16,000 for Anthropic, the server’s own for others.

twoFactor.title: Two-factor authentication
twoFactor.codePrompt: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
twoFactor.recoveryPrompt: Enter one of the recovery codes you saved when you turned on two-factor authentication.
twoFactor.requiredHint: This workspace requires two-factor authentication. Set up an authenticator app, such as Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator or 1Password, to continue.
twoFactor.scanHint: Scan this QR code with your authenticator app, then enter the 6-digit code it shows.
twoFactor.qrLabel: QR code for the authenticator app
twoFactor.keyHint: Can't scan it? Enter this key in the app instead:
twoFactor.recoveryHint: Keep these codes somewhere safe. Each one signs you in once if you lose your phone, and this is the only time they are shown.
twoFactor.sectionHint: Ask for a code from an authenticator app each time you sign in, as well as your password.
twoFactor.sectionRequired: This workspace requires two-factor authentication, so it stays on.
twoFactor.turnOffHint: Enter a code from your authenticator app to confirm. Your recovery codes stop working too.
twoFactor.newCodesHint: Enter a code from your authenticator app. Your old recovery codes stop working.

spaceArchive.banner: This space is archived, so it is read-only. Nothing in it can change until someone who manages it restores it.
spaceArchive.archiveHint: The space becomes read-only and leaves space lists, ticket pickers and dashboards. Notifications, Git webhooks and automations stop. Links to its tickets keep working, and you can restore it at any time.
spaceArchive.restoreHint: The space becomes editable again, exactly as it was when it was archived, and comes back to space lists and pickers.
spaceArchive.deleteHint: Only an archived space can be deleted, by an admin. It waits in the trash for a grace period, where an admin can restore it. After that its tickets, comments, attachments, sprints, boards, workflows, Git links, assistant conversations and notifications are removed for good, and its key is free again.
spaceArchive.deleteNeedsArchive: Archive the space before you delete it.
spaceArchive.restoredFromTrash: Space restored from the trash. It stays archived.
